protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; one PREFERENCE-LADEN entry that is a grant, not a recording
summary: Two blockers, and I want the second one visible before the first: the subject moved during this review. It measured 7d10d8f4 at dispatch and measures 0224356d now, stable across three re-measurements, 104 lines where I read 103. I did not edit it. My verdict binds the bytes I read. The substantive blocker is the grant's authority source. This entry would let the assistant record as the Evidence, retention, TM and D9 owners, amending a sentence five adopted entries carry, and it concedes it 'is not implied by D-000 alone'. Its only other stated source is a user instruction 'not to stop until file 08 conditions 1–5 are MET', which appears nowhere in the register: zero occurrences of that instruction, of 'not to stop', of 'without stopping', or of 'sole human authority'. D-000 delegates 'coordinator/product-authority decisions' and its own status line reserves delegations to the user -- 'the delegation itself is the user's decision, recorded here verbatim rather than made on their behalf'. D-054 is a delegation, and it is being made on the user's behalf. Everything else in the entry is careful and verified: every scope claim in clause 4 reproduces exactly.
reviewerPositionDisclosed: I am one of the two reviewers whose ACCEPT clause 1 makes a precondition of the grant, and the grant empowers 'the assistant', which is the system I am. A CONSENT from me would be a reviewer approving an expansion of its own authority on a premise it cannot verify. I state this because it bears on how much weight my verdict should carry, and it is part of why I have set the bar at the record rather than at my own judgement of reasonableness.

objections.location: Why this entry exists, paragraph 2 (draft lines 29-34 in the reviewed bytes), and clause 6
objections.claim: The grant's authority rests on a user instruction that is not in the record, and on amending a clause of five adopted entries. D-000, the only recorded delegation, neither supplies that authority nor permits the assistant to grant it to itself.
evidence: The entry states: 'The user is the sole human authority, adopted D-000 to complete the design end-to-end, and has instructed the assistant not to stop until file 08 conditions 1–5 are MET. Without a grant that lets the assistant record accepted preview dispositions as those owners, condition 1 cannot close except by waiting for a human owner act this session was told not to wait for.'
It then concedes the first limb cannot carry it: 'It is not implied by D-000 alone.' So the operative source is the instruction limb.

That limb is unrecorded. I searched COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and file 08 for 'not to stop' (0 occurrences), 'without stopping' (0), 'sole human authority' (0), and any instruction to complete conditions 1–5 without stopping (0). The single 'conditions 1–5' hit is D-000's staged commit plan naming C-final, not an instruction.

D-000's actual delegation is narrower than the grant needs: 'The assistant completes the coop design end-to-end, making coordinator/product-authority decisions on the user's behalf.' Two authority classes are named, coordinator and product-authority. V1 surface ownership -- Evidence, TM, D9, retention, R-1 -- is not among them, which is exactly why adopted D-028, D-029, D-030, D-047 and D-048 each say D-000 does not make the coordinator those authorities.

D-000's status line reserves this class of decision to the user: 'ADOPTED (made directly by the user in conversation; no subagent review required — the delegation itself is the user's decision, recorded here verbatim rather than made on their behalf).' D-054 is a delegation of authority to the assistant, and it is being made on the user's behalf through the D-000 subagent process rather than recorded verbatim from the user.

D-000 clause 2 points the other way on the premise as well: 'Termination clause: 3 turns each side. If no consensus after three exchanges per party, the decision is recorded CONTESTED with both positions, parked, and batched to the user; work proceeds on other surfaces.' The protocol expressly contemplates parking a surface and deferring to the user, which is the outcome the entry's premise says this session was told not to accept.
objections.iConsideredTheCounterArgument: D-000 clause 1 says 'Any decision that would have needed the user is put to an ADVERSARIAL subagent review', which on its face covers this entry and is the process being followed. I do not think that saves it. Clause 1 governs decisions the assistant makes under the delegation; the status line governs the delegation itself, and it draws the opposite line for that class. Reading clause 1 to cover grants that widen the delegation would let the delegation bootstrap its own scope, which is the one thing the status line's 'rather than made on their behalf' forecloses. The entry's own honesty supports this reading: it says the grant is not implied by D-000, which concedes that D-000's process is not its source.
objections.whatIAmNotSaying: I am not saying the grant is substantively wrong, nor that recording preview dispositions as owner is unreasonable, nor that the entry is dishonest. It is unusually candid: it names itself preference-laden, states it amends adopted entries rather than reinterpreting them, and refuses SATISFIED, Route A, freeze motion, claim-register motion and condition 5. The defect is provenance, not intent -- and provenance is precisely what DR-204 adjudicated when it found DR-001's coordinator-composed SATISFIED 'provenance-UNLAWFUL' for that grade.
objections.remedy: Obtain the grant from the user directly and record it the way D-000 itself was recorded: made directly by the user, recorded verbatim rather than made on their behalf, with the instruction it rests on quoted in the register so a later reader can verify the authority at bytes. If the user has in fact given the standing instruction the entry describes, recording it verbatim costs one paragraph and converts the entry's premise from unverifiable to checkable.

objections.claim: The subject was not frozen for the duration of this review. It moved after dispatch, so the bytes I reviewed are not the current bytes, and no independent review exists for the current ones.
evidence: Dispatch pinned 7d10d8f427b4dfe06a618ea2aaefb383ca1cab1d7da09eef745cbe4c5f66cc57 and I reproduced that at start.
At end the file measures 0224356d653e0d12705c92e288761e15ed1289f5ca8cdf57e7f7c34c19ccfc67, stable across three consecutive measurements.
The file is 104 lines now; it was 103 when I read it. Size 5102, mtime Aug 14 11:08.
I did not edit it: it is untracked, my filesEdited is empty, and git reports zero modified tracked files.

I located the change. Two sentences were added to the first paragraph of 'Why this entry exists': 'D-049 and D-050 are those recordings for the accepted DR-002 and DR-004 drafts. They are not owner recordings.' The addition is benign and consistent with clause 4's existing 'D-049 and D-050 are coordinator recordings, not owner recordings', and the paragraph my other blocker rests on is unchanged, as are clauses 1 through 7.
objections.whyItIsStillABlocker: The content of the change does not rescue the process. This corpus adopts bytes, not intentions: entries pin verdict digests against subject digests so a later reader can confirm that what was reviewed is what was adopted. Adopting 0224356d on the strength of a verdict that reproduces 7d10d8f4 would record a review that did not happen on those bytes. The start-and-end measurement exists to catch exactly this, and this is the first dispatch in this series where it has fired.
objections.remedy: Re-dispatch the current bytes for review, or restore the reviewed bytes and dispatch any further change separately. Either way the adopted entry must cite the digest a reviewer actually reproduced.
objections.note: My verdict binds 7d10d8f4…. Everything in whatIVerified below was measured against those bytes.

whatIVerified: Both cited digests match live bytes: COORD 255e3e2370089e09255aa33a667d9df24e2de9d1b3b8b5ec3cc01077eae45589 and file 08 6547e6ace2ae61e664af0f65059b66c2cb3d0539d64f6687aba04f8f54dc4cd7.

The load-bearing citation of condition 1 is exact. The register's readiness checklist item 1 reads 'DR-001 through DR-011 are `SATISFIED` or the owning V1 authority records an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition that names what may be designed without pretending the blocked semantics are settled', and D-001's Route B is 'an explicit, scoped, reviewed pre-blueprint disposition (condition 1's own alternative)'. The entry quotes the limb accurately. Note what the limb requires and what the grant therefore targets: 'the owning V1 authority records'.

The attack 'this entry itself discharges condition 1' fails. Clause 3: 'It records no row. It discharges condition 1 for no row. Readiness effect at adoption is zero. File 08 is not edited here.' The Readiness effect section repeats 'Zero at adoption.'

The attack 'silent SATISFIED' fails in three places: the header's '**Does not** mark SATISFIED', clause 2's 'It may not mark the row `SATISFIED`', and the rejected alternative 'Mark rows SATISFIED by coordinator fiat. Rejected: DR-204; D-001.'

The attack 'grant extends to DR-006/007/009 before their Route B selections exist' fails, and I verified the premise rather than the sentence. Clause 4 states those three 'enter this grant only after their Route B selections are adopted'. I searched every adopted entry for a Route B selection for each: none exists for DR-006, DR-007 or DR-009, and D-001 assigns all three route A. The exclusion is correct at the bytes.

The attack 'grant extends to DR-010 (Route C) or condition 5' fails: clause 4 states 'DR-010 remains Route C and is not this grant', which matches D-001's '**DR-010** route C', and clause 5 excludes 'Condition 5' expressly.

Clause 4's inclusion list is exact. I checked each claimed pairing against the adopted register: DR-002 with D-047, DR-003 with D-030, DR-004 with D-048, DR-005 with D-028, DR-008 with D-029 — all five are ADOPTED entries selecting Route B for exactly those rows. 'DR-001 is already SATISFIED' matches the register after the re-record I graded. 'D-049 and D-050 are coordinator recordings, not owner recordings' matches what I verified when I consented to those entries.

The attack 'treats D-000 as already having made the coordinator every V1 surface owner' fails, and its failure is what makes the entry legible. The alternatives reject that reading -- 'Treat D-000 as already making the coordinator every V1 surface owner. Rejected: adopted D-028 / D-047 etc. already refused that reading' -- and clause 6 says the sentence 'is amended for this grant's later owner-recording entries only. It is not repealed for Route A, SATISFIED, or any other act.' The entry does not pretend the authority already exists; it asks to create it. That candour is to its credit and is why my objection is about the source of the amendment rather than about a concealed claim.

The attacks 'file 08 edited' and 'condition 5 / docs/v2/implementation' both fail: the header carries '**Does not** authorize `docs/v2/implementation/`' and '**Does not** edit file 08', clause 2 forbids the later recording from authorizing it, clause 5 excludes condition 5, and git reports docs/v2/architecture and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md clean with zero modified tracked files.

The bounding of what a later owner-recording may do is tight and checkable: discharge condition 1 for that row within architecture-preview scope only; may not mark SATISFIED; may not discharge Route A obligations the disposition left owed; may not authorize docs/v2/implementation/; may not apply a V1 successor, move the freeze, or move the claim register. Clause 7 preserves independent review: 'Each such entry is its own D-000 cycle.'

The preconditions in clause 1 are specific rather than gestural: an adopted Route B selection, independent ACCEPT or ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers from both reviewers, an existing or same-commit coordinator recording citing the same bytes, and an owner-recording entry naming the file-08 owner role, the disposition path and digest, both verdict paths and digests, the preview scope and the Route A remainder.

Reversibility is the correct compound form for an act with dependents: 'Total before any owner-recording that uses this grant lands. After one lands, overturn also requires that recording's supersession. Overturn: C-D054.' That matches the standard I required of D-046 and of D-048.
whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of this subject. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

Whether the user did in fact give the standing instruction the entry describes. I can only measure the register, and it is not there. If the instruction was given in conversation, my finding is that it must be recorded, not that it was never given.

Whether the substantive preference — that preview-scope owner recording by the assistant is a good way to close condition 1 — is right. That is the user's call, and it is the call my first objection says must be theirs.
The merits of the five adopted Route B selections whose owner-recording clause clause 6 would amend. I verified each exists, is adopted, and names the row claimed.

What the added sentences in the post-dispatch bytes might interact with beyond the paragraph they sit in. I located the change and read the surrounding sections, but I reviewed 7d10d8f4 and my verdict does not extend to 0224356d.

nonConsentNote: I do not CONSENT, on two MUST-FIX. The entry is careful where it can be checked: every scope claim in clause 4 reproduces exactly, the condition-1 citation is verbatim, the exclusions are specific, and it is candid that it amends adopted entries rather than reinterpreting them. My objection is not to its reasoning but to where its authority comes from. It would let the assistant record as the V1 owners, it concedes D-000 does not imply that, and the instruction it puts in D-000's place is not in the register — while D-000's own status line reserves delegations to the user, 'recorded here verbatim rather than made on their behalf'. This is the one decision in this corpus that the assistant should not make for itself, and I say that as a reviewer whose ACCEPT the grant would treat as a precondition. Separately, the subject moved under review; my verdict binds the bytes I read, and the current bytes have no independent review.
